factions.name: The Order of Theia
factions.rightAbout: The threat is real and the ritual works.
factions.wrongAbout: The current system is the only possible solution.
factions.summary: The Order has safeguarded the Colony since its founding, believing stability must be preserved even when mercy looks like cruelty.
factions.origin: The Colony needed caretakers willing to preserve the ritual and protect people from the unbearable weight of memory. Protectors became rulers when preservation and authority became indistinguishable.
factions.publicFace: The ruling authority of the Colony.
factions.selfImage: The necessary shield between the Colony and collapse.
factions.notes: The Order of Theia's name derives from Aletheia - though no one remembers this, she's the first name in the book.
factions.history:
The Order of Theia began as a small circle of caretakers entrusted with preserving the ritual at the heart of the Colony's survival. Their work was not understood as rule, law, or government, but as vigilance. Someone had to guard the Book of Names, prepare the Ritual Chamber, and ensure the burden was carried before its weight became too great for the Colony to endure. The first members of the Order did not think of themselves as rulers. They were guardians standing between ordinary people and a truth too heavy to bear.

Over generations, preservation became administration. Every practical question eventually touched the ritual, and the Order answered those questions one by one—not through conquest, but through necessity. The Hall of the Keepers became the center of civic life, where disputes were settled and traditions interpreted, while the Bell of the Sun gave the Order's decisions public voice. The ritual remained hidden, but the authority built around it became visible throughout the Colony.

Today, the Order can no longer distinguish between preserving the Colony and preserving its own institutions. Its members sincerely believe they stand between civilization and collapse, and they are not entirely wrong. The ritual has protected the Colony for generations, reinforcing the conviction that stability itself is proof of righteousness. What began as a duty to safeguard the burden has become a certainty that no other future can be trusted.

Even now, many within the Order are disciplined, compassionate people carrying an impossible responsibility. They conceal the truth not from cruelty, but from the belief that some burdens destroy those unprepared to bear them. The name Theia itself reflects that transformation—a fragment of Aletheia, the first name recorded in the Book, whose meaning has long since been forgotten. The Order was founded to preserve a truth it can no longer speak, and over time, preserving that truth became preserving the silence around it.

factions.name: Heirs
factions.rightAbout: The compromise was imposed on them
factions.afraidOf: Becoming the next generation of caretakers
factions.wrongAbout: The past can simply be discarded

factions.name: Witnesses
factions.rightAbout: The Colony is losing sight of its cost, and no sacrifice should be allowed to become invisible.
factions.wrongAbout: They mistake preservation for healing, and do not realize that by removing the visible wounds of forgetting, they help the Colony survive its own moral injury.
factions.response: Remember the cost. No sacrifice should disappear into anonymity. A burden forgotten becomes a burden repeated.
factions.summary: A sanctioned branch within the Order, the Witnesses preserve the belongings, stories, and traces of the Forgotten, offering dignity to those the ritual erases while unknowingly making the ritual’s aftermath bearable enough to continue.
factions.origin: Members of the Order argued that sacrifice must be witnessed and remembered, not merely administered and concealed. Reformers became historians when tolerated dissent hardened into official remembrance.
factions.publicFace: Quiet archivists, memorialists, and tradition-keepers under the Order's umbrella.
factions.selfImage: The Colony's conscience, trained to look where others look away.
factions.history:
The Witnesses began as a protest of conscience within the earliest structures of the Order. The ritual may have been necessary, but some could not accept that necessity required silence. If a person willingly carried the burden for the sake of the Colony, then their passing deserved more than administration. It deserved reverence. The first Witnesses did not seek to end the ritual. They sought to ensure that every sacrifice was seen, honored, and mourned.

What began as quiet acts of remembrance gradually became a solemn responsibility. The Witnesses gathered letters, tools, jewelry, unfinished artwork, and other belongings left behind by the Forgotten, preserving them within the Hall of Remembrance and recording them in the Ledger. Though names inevitably faded from the record, the objects themselves endured. Over time, the Witnesses came to recognize that some possessions carried more than memory. Items burdened with profound emotional weight could leave subtle fractures in the world around them, unsettling those who encountered them. Preserving these relics became not only an act of remembrance, but an act of stewardship, keeping dangerous wounds from quietly spreading through the Colony.

As their duties expanded, the Witnesses established the House of Abiding, where those chosen for the ritual spend their final days in peace while their belongings are gathered for preservation before memory fades. Their ceremonies evolved as well. The Empty Lectern became the center of memorial services where the stories of the Forgotten could be spoken aloud, even as the names themselves disappeared from every page and every mind. In this way, the Witnesses sought to preserve dignity where identity could not survive.

Today, the Witnesses remain the Colony's conscience, preserving the traces of lives that would otherwise disappear entirely. Their halls hold generations of forgotten belongings, each catalogued with painstaking care, while the Ledger continues to grow despite its empty spaces. They believe no sacrifice should vanish without remembrance, even if they have come to accept that remembrance itself cannot change the burden they faithfully record.

factions.name: Fractured
factions.wrongAbout: Their conclusions are often distorted by incomplete information
factions.origin: They are often created by unresolved contact with emotionally resonant belongings, especially practical objects redistributed after the ritual that accidentally return to people or places connected to the Forgotten.

factions.name: The Dawn Assembly
factions.coreTenet: There must be a better way.
factions.certainOf: The current system is unjust and must be changed.
factions.rightAbout: The compromise is morally unacceptable, and responsibility cannot remain concentrated in hidden institutions.
factions.wrongAbout: They mistake visible improvement for systemic transformation, making the Colony more humane without necessarily making it free.
factions.response: Share the cost. The burden belongs to everyone. Healing begins when responsibility is carried together rather than assigned to one person.
factions.summary: Once a secret revolutionary gathering beyond the Colony walls, the Dawn Assembly is now a legitimate civic reform movement seeking change through politics, debate, and coalition-building.
factions.origin: Frustration with sanctioned remembrance pushed citizens to meet in secret at dawn and imagine a Colony beyond the Order's control. Revolutionaries became politicians when secrecy gave way to legitimacy.
factions.publicFace: The respectable reform party of the Colony.
factions.selfImage: The patient architects of a better tomorrow.
factions.history:
The Dawn Assembly began among Witnesses who could no longer bear the distance between remembrance and change. They had spent years honoring the Forgotten, preserving their belongings, and comforting the grieving, only to watch the ritual continue year after year. Over time, some came to a painful conclusion: the Colony had learned how to mourn without transforming. They believed remembrance was not enough. The burden belonged to everyone, and the future could not simply become another repetition of the past.

Their earliest gatherings took place before sunrise in workshops, courtyards, and unfinished public spaces beyond the reach of the Order. Dawn became both a meeting time and a symbol of the future they hoped to build. What began as quiet conversations soon grew into organized petitions, public proposals, and open criticism of the Colony's oldest institutions. They believed the ritual's burden should be shared rather than concealed, and that a better society could be built through collective responsibility rather than inherited tradition.

Over time, the movement became too popular to ignore. The Assembly Hall gave the Dawn a legitimate place within civic life, while the Dawn Charter transformed scattered demands into a living record of reforms and aspirations. Through the Civic Improvement Fund and the Public Works Yard, the Assembly proved its ideals through roads, bridges, schools, gardens, and public works that improved daily life throughout the Colony. They did not merely argue for a better future. They began building one.

Today, the Dawn Assembly remains the Colony's most credible political alternative to the Order, advocating gradual reform, public accountability, and shared responsibility for the burden. Yet each success has carried an unexpected cost. As the Assembly became part of civic life, it also became part of the system it once opposed. The Colony grew more compassionate, more prosperous, and more hopeful—but the ritual endured all the same.

factions.name: Civilians
factions.rightAbout: Somebody has to keep society functioning

factions.name: Shattered
factions.coreTenet: A system built on sacrifice has no legitimacy.
factions.certainOf: No institution in the Colony can redeem itself.
factions.rightAbout: The system is morally abhorrent, and generations of reform have failed to end it.
factions.afraidOf: False hope, co-option, and becoming complicit.
factions.response: Destroy it. The price isn't worth it.
factions.summary: The youngest faction in the Colony, the Shattered are a clandestine movement of the disillusioned, using hidden shelters, dead drops, and fractured objects to reopen wounds the Colony has learned to ignore.
factions.origin: Generations of stalled reform convinced younger citizens that the Assembly had become part of the machine it once opposed. Idealists became radicals when hope curdled into proof that the whole system must break.
factions.selfImage: The only people honest enough to stop bargaining with evil.
factions.history:
The Shattered are the youngest faction in the Colony, born from the same wound that once created the Dawn Assembly. Where the Dawn looked at the Witnesses and said, "Mourning is not enough," the Shattered looked at the Dawn and said, "Reform is not enough." They grew up surrounded by public hearings, revised charters, and promises of change, yet watched the ritual continue year after year. To them, the Assembly did not fail because it lacked good intentions. It failed because the system learned how to survive reform.

Many of the earliest Shattered were former Dawn organizers, frustrated apprentices, grieving families, and members of the Fractured whose lives had been shaped by absences no one else could explain. They began not as a formal movement, but as conversations held after meetings ended—in back rooms, abandoned cellars, and forgotten corners of the Colony. The Broken Bell became their refuge: public enough to hide in plain sight, disreputable enough to be ignored, and broken enough to feel honest. Rejecting councils, charters, and institutions, they instead built hidden stockpiles, dead drops, and whispered networks that could survive without leaders.

Their greatest discovery was not political, but personal. It came through the Fractured Objects left behind by the Forgotten. They learned that certain belongings carried more than sentimental value; returned to the right place, they could awaken grief without memory and certainty without explanation. The Shattered realized the Colony could ignore arguments and absorb reform, but it struggled to ignore the wounds it had buried. Rather than persuading people with ideology, they learned to recruit through absence, placing forgotten echoes where they would be felt most deeply.

Today, the Shattered remain a decentralized movement of saboteurs, smugglers, and disillusioned idealists convinced that every institution eventually forgets why it was created. They reject compromise as another form of surrender, believing that every hidden cost must eventually be brought into the light. When they speak of the Reckoning, they do not mean vengeance. They mean that every burden comes due, every compromise demands payment, and every wound the Colony refuses to heal will one day reopen on its own.

factions.name: EGRESS Institute
factions.coreTenet: No burden is immutable if it can be understood.
factions.certainOf: The solution has not yet been discovered.
factions.rightAbout: The phenomenon has rules, and those rules can be observed, tested, and partially understood.
factions.wrongAbout: They mistake measurement for mastery and knowledge for wisdom.
factions.response: Surpass the cost. The burden is not a moral condition to be accepted, but a technical problem to be solved.
factions.summary: The EGRESS Institute studies memory, ritual, and reality distortion through engram storage, controlled experimentation, and long-term observation, pursuing mastery over the mechanism even when its ethical consequences are ignored.
factions.origin: Scholars concluded that theology, politics, and remembrance alone could not resolve the Colony's metaphysical crisis. Only disciplined inquiry could reveal the laws governing memory itself. Over generations, understanding ceased to be the goal. Instead, knowledge became merely the means through which power was pursued.
factions.publicFace: Brilliant but unsettling scholars with dangerous equipment and better funding than restraint.
factions.selfImage: The only adults trying to solve the actual problem.
factions.notes: EGRESS stands for "Engram Generation, Restoration, Evaluation, and Storage Systems."
factions.motto: Transcending the Limits of the Mind
factions.history:
A loose fellowship of scholars, physicians, natural philosophers, and curious minds began gathering to study the strange phenomena surrounding the Colony long before the EGRESS Institute existed. While others sought to preserve, reform, or escape the burden, these early researchers treated it as a puzzle waiting to be solved. They catalogued memory disturbances, investigated fractured objects, interviewed survivors of Veiled encounters, and documented the subtle ways reality shifted around the Forgotten. They believed the ritual was not beyond understanding—only beyond current knowledge.

Everything changed with the discovery of the first Engrams: preserved fragments of memory captured before the ritual dispersed them completely. Though incapable of preserving identity or names, these fragments retained thoughts, sensations, habits, and emotional impressions, proving that memory itself could be isolated, stored, and studied. The discovery transformed an informal community of investigators into a dedicated institution. They named it EGRESS—Engram Generation, Restoration, Evaluation, and Storage Systems—reflecting a new conviction that the burden could eventually be understood through disciplined observation and experimentation.

Over the generations, discovery gave way to accumulation. The Engram Vault grew into a hidden archive containing centuries of preserved memories, while the Research Archive expanded into the Colony's largest collection of experiments, observations, and theoretical work on the ritual and the Veiled. As the Institute's understanding deepened, Veiled Containment transformed rare manifestations from inexplicable encounters into controlled subjects of study. EGRESS gradually became the foremost authority on the mechanics of memory, reality, and the burden itself.

Today, the Institute may understand more about the Colony's hidden truths than any other faction. Its researchers possess generations of evidence, preserved memories, and experimental results that could reshape the Colony's understanding of itself. Yet EGRESS remains reluctant to act on what it has learned. The Institute was founded in the belief that understanding would become the Colony's egress—its way out of the burden. Over generations, that purpose quietly inverted.

Once, they pursued understanding in order to find an exit. Now, they preserve the exit in order to pursue understanding. The work is never finished, because there is always one more observation to make, one more variable to isolate, one more unanswered question that might finally complete the picture. The Institute still believes understanding is the way out. It has simply forgotten that 'out' was ever the destination.

factions.name: Cult of the Unknown
factions.certainOf: The truth has been concealed because the powerful fear it.
factions.rightAbout: The Order suppresses information, and the Colony's understanding is incomplete.
factions.wrongAbout: They mistake mystery for benevolence and revelation for salvation.
factions.response: Embrace it. The burden is not merely a curse — it is sacred, transformative, and perhaps even necessary.
factions.summary: The Cult of the Unknown reveres what the Colony fears, offering hospitality, pilgrimage, and ritual surrender to those who believe the Veiled are not monsters but invitations.
factions.origin: Fragments revealed by reformers and Witness records inspired some citizens to treat the hidden force with reverence rather than fear. Seekers became clergy when wonder hardened into doctrine.
factions.publicFace: A strange but hospitable pilgrim faith drawn to forbidden places, unsettling visions, and acts of voluntary surrender.
factions.selfImage: Pilgrims brave enough to approach what the Colony has demonized.
factions.history:
The Cult of the Unknown began as a loose fellowship of Seekers who believed the Colony had mistaken mystery for danger. While others debated the burden as a political or moral problem, these early adherents became captivated by the strange experiences surrounding the ritual itself. They collected dreams, survivor accounts, moments of déjà vu, and stories of places where reality seemed thin, believing that understanding required encounter rather than explanation. Many wandered the Duskwood in silence, fasted, meditated, or sought solitude in places marked by lingering absence, convinced that the Unknown was not merely to be feared, but approached.

The Cult came to see the Veiled manifestations not as invaders, but as Pilgrims—beings moving toward a destination the Colony had forgotten. Their gatherings gradually transformed into acts of pilgrimage and devotion. Pilgrim's Rest became a sanctuary for travelers, mystics, and the spiritually wounded, with rooms kept prepared for guests who might never arrive. The Duskwood Shrine marked places where the boundary between worlds felt especially thin, drawing those willing to seek revelation beyond the safety of the Colony.

The Offering Chest grew from the Cult's imperfect understanding of fractured objects: belongings of the Forgotten that sometimes carry enough emotional weight to wound reality itself. Believing the power lay in sacrifice rather than history, Cult pilgrims began surrendering treasured possessions in the hope that a freely chosen absence might create the same connection to the Unknown. Their greatest collection, the Face of the Unknown, preserves hundreds of paintings, sculptures, carvings, and tapestries created by those who claim to have glimpsed the Veiled. No two depictions agree, and the Cult considers that disagreement itself to be sacred. Every vision is believed to reveal only one fragment of a reality too vast for any single witness to comprehend.

Over generations, seeking became ritual, ritual became faith, and faith became doctrine. Today, the Cult of the Unknown offers hospitality to pilgrims, refuge to those whose experiences defy explanation, and reverence toward mysteries the rest of the Colony would rather contain. Its members believe that surrender, encounter, and devotion draw them closer to the truth hidden beyond the Veil, even if they cannot yet understand what waits there.

factions.name: Aspis
factions.coreTenet: Every system must be made useful, stable, and accountable.
factions.certainOf: Every system can be managed if its obligations are understood.
factions.rightAbout: The Colony cannot survive moral transformation without logistical continuity.
factions.response: Use it. If the burden exists, it has value. Stability, knowledge, and power should not be wasted.
factions.summary: Aspis arrived as merchants and remained as administrators, discovering that the ritual breaks contracts, ownership, inheritance, and debt as surely as it breaks memory. Their presence in the Colony is exploitative, but also stabilizing: they preserve the systems of obligation that allow trade, food, property, and civic life to continue.
factions.origin: Aspis established a trading post to exploit the Colony's strategic location, only to discover that its true value lay in the impossible challenges it posed to commerce.
factions.history:
Aspis arrived in the Colony as merchants, drawn by the opportunity of a prosperous independent settlement straddling the border between Andoran and Isger. Its agents expected to find a profitable trade hub, rich in commerce but otherwise unremarkable. The Colony's traditions were dismissed as local custom, its rituals as harmless superstition, and its politics as another landscape to navigate. They did not come seeking the burden. They came seeking opportunity.

Everything changed when the books stopped balancing. Debtors vanished from memory. Contracts lost their signatories. Property ownership became impossible to reconcile. Businesses continued operating despite having no traceable founders. Commerce depends upon continuity, and the ritual quietly undermined every assumption on which trade was built. What began as a commercial venture became a centuries-long effort to understand how a functioning economy could survive in a society where identity itself was unstable.

The River Exchange grew into the Colony's primary connection to the outside world, while the Docks became the artery through which food, supplies, and commerce continued to flow. To preserve the web of obligations the ritual continually unraveled, Aspis established the Clearing House, developing legal and financial systems capable of reconciling debts, contracts, inheritances, and property despite the erosion of memory. Behind it all, the Claims Registry quietly accumulated generations of commercial anomalies, becoming one of the most complete records of how the ritual reshapes the Colony's legal and economic foundations.

Today, Aspis presents itself as a practical partner in the Colony's prosperity, providing trade, credit, logistics, and administrative stability while remaining largely indifferent to the philosophical disputes consuming the other factions. Its methods are unapologetically self-interested, but its systems have become indispensable.

The systems developed within the Colony have become valuable far beyond its borders. Every improvement to the Clearing House, every refinement to the Claims Registry, and every new method of preserving obligation despite uncertainty strengthens the Consortium's ability to conduct commerce throughout Golarion. To Aspis, the Colony is no longer merely a profitable trade outpost—it is the proving ground for a more resilient world.

assets.name: Assembly Hall
assets.description: The recognized home of the Dawn Assembly, where proposals are debated, public hearings are held, and visions for the Colony's future are shaped. Though the Order retains ultimate authority, the Assembly Hall remains the center of civic discourse and reform.

assets.name: Bell of the Sun
assets.description: Hung above the central square, the Bell of the Sun marks moments of civic importance. For two centuries, its voice has carried the authority of the Order.

assets.name: Book of Names
assets.description: The oldest and most closely guarded artifact in the Colony. It records those who have borne the burden, preserving the continuity of the ritual across generations.

assets.name: Civic Improvement Fund
assets.description: A treasury reserved exclusively for projects that improve the lives of the Colony's citizens. Roads, bridges, schools, gardens, and public works are all financed through the Fund, making it one of the Assembly's most effective tools for turning ideals into visible change.

assets.name: Claims Registry
assets.description: A confidential archive documenting property ownership, contractual obligations, inheritance disputes, and centuries of unresolved commercial anomalies. Though created to keep the Consortium's books balanced, the Registry has become one of the most complete records of how the ritual quietly reshapes the Colony's legal and economic foundations.

assets.name: Clearing House
assets.description: A network of offices responsible for reconciling contracts, transferring property, settling debts, and maintaining commercial continuity despite the Colony's unique circumstances. Here, obligations are preserved even when memory cannot be.

assets.name: Dawn Charter
assets.description: A living document that records every reform ever proposed by the Dawn Assembly. Amendments, revisions, and generations of commentary fill its pages, reflecting the belief that no society is ever truly finished and every generation should leave the Colony better than they found it.

assets.name: Dawn Press
assets.description: Printing presses and organizing offices producing the Dawn Assembly’s notices, petitions, campaign materials, and reform publications.

assets.name: Dead Drop Network
assets.description: A distributed network of concealed message caches hidden throughout the Colony. Loose stones, hollow beams, forgotten wells, and other unremarkable places serve as silent exchanges for information, allowing the Shattered to communicate without relying on any single courier or meeting place.

assets.name: Docks
assets.description: Warehouses, piers, cranes, and loading yards lining the Colony's riverfront. Control of the docks determines the movement of food, supplies, and commerce, making them one of the most strategically important pieces of infrastructure in the Colony.

assets.name: Duskwood Shrine
assets.description: A secluded shrine hidden deep within the Duskwood, where the boundary between the familiar and the unknown is believed to grow thin. Adherents journey here to meditate, leave offerings, and seek moments of quiet communion with the mysteries beyond the Colony.

assets.name: EGRESS Institute
assets.description: The headquarters of the Engram Generation, Restoration, Evaluation, and Storage Systems Institute. Laboratories, lecture halls, workshops, and research facilities fill its halls, serving as the Colony's foremost center for the study of memory, identity, and the metaphysical phenomena surrounding the Veil. Its integrated Research Archive preserves two centuries of field reports, experimental results, recovered observations, failed hypotheses, and unanswered questions.

assets.name: Engram Vault
assets.description: A secure archive containing generations of preserved memory engrams recovered before the ritual. Though stripped of names and disconnected from identity, these records preserve fragments of the Forgotten's thoughts, experiences, and personalities, offering EGRESS an unparalleled opportunity to study the nature of memory itself.

assets.name: Face of the Unknown
assets.description: A growing collection of sculptures, paintings, carvings, tapestries, and other works created by pilgrims attempting to depict what they have witnessed beyond the veil. No two representations agree, yet the Cult believes each reveals a fragment of a greater truth. Together, they are known simply as the Face of the Unknown.

assets.name: Hall of Remembrance
assets.description: A sanctuary where the belongings of the Forgotten are preserved with reverence. Here the Witnesses catalog, safeguard, and honor the traces of lives that can no longer be remembered.

assets.name: Hall of the Keepers
assets.description: The administrative heart of the Colony, where the Order governs, adjudicates disputes, and oversees the countless duties required to preserve two centuries of continuity.

assets.name: Hidden Stockpiles
assets.description: A decentralized network of caches hidden throughout abandoned buildings, forgotten cellars, and secluded ruins. Stocked with food, medicine, tools, and other necessities.

assets.name: House of Abiding
assets.description: A quiet residence where Those Who Abide spend their final days before the ritual. Their belongings are carefully gathered here so they may be preserved once memory has passed from the world.

assets.name: Occlusion Containment
assets.description: A restricted research facility where captured Veiled and other anomalous phenomena are studied under controlled conditions. To EGRESS, understanding the Unknown is the surest path toward protecting the Colony—even if that pursuit requires experiments few others would consider acceptable.

assets.name: Order Watch Garrison
assets.description: The Order’s watch barracks and guard deployment facilities, supporting patrols, civic security, and enforcement of Order decisions.

assets.name: Pilgrim's Rest
assets.description: A welcoming sanctuary that offers food, shelter, and quiet hospitality to pilgrims, travelers, and seekers alike. Several rooms are intentionally kept prepared for the Pilgrims should they ever arrive, their beds made and lanterns lit despite centuries of remaining unoccupied.

assets.name: Public Works Yard
assets.description: Workshops, warehouses, and planning offices dedicated to the continual improvement of the Colony. From road repairs and irrigation projects to new public buildings, nearly every civic improvement begins here before spreading into the streets beyond.

assets.name: Recovery Wagons
assets.description: Wagons and transport supplies used by the Witnesses to recover, convey, and safeguard belongings associated with the Forgotten.

assets.name: River Exchange
assets.description: The Consortium's administrative and commercial headquarters, where trade entering or leaving the Colony is negotiated, inspected, and recorded. More than a marketplace, the River Exchange serves as the Colony's primary connection to Andoran, Isger, and the wider world beyond its borders.

assets.name: Scientific Charter
assets.description: A formal grant recognizing EGRESS’s authority to investigate mnemonic phenomena and conduct research in service of the Colony.

assets.name: The Broken Bell
assets.description: An aging tavern on the edge of respectability whose faded sign depicts a bell long since broken away. Its common room welcomes anyone, but those who know to ask are quietly shown to the back, where the Shattered exchange information, plan operations, and offer sanctuary to those who have lost faith in the Colony.

assets.name: The Empty Lectern
assets.description: During each remembrance, the Ledger is placed upon this lectern and passages describing the recovered belongings of the Forgotten are read aloud. When the ceremony concludes, the Ledger is returned to the Hall, leaving the lectern empty until the next ritual.

assets.name: The Ledger
assets.description: An ever-growing inventory of the belongings entrusted to the Hall of Remembrance. Every entry records where an object was found, signs of its use, and the traces of the life that surrounded it—but never a name. Attempts to record names invariably fade, smear, or become unreadable, and generations ago the Witnesses stopped trying.

assets.name: The Offering Chest
assets.description: A collection of deeply personal possessions voluntarily surrendered by those seeking communion with the Unknown. The Cult believes that relinquishing something precious creates space within the soul for revelation, though whether these offerings possess any greater significance remains a matter of faith.

assets.name: The Ritual Chamber
assets.description: The sacred chamber where the annual ritual is performed. Few have entered it, fewer still understand it, and none speak openly of what transpires within.

assets.name: The Unclaimed Object
assets.description: A newly-identified Fractured Object. It originally belonged to [Party member]; its mnemonic weight comes from its connection to someone subsequently Forgotten. Its form and the identities involved remain to be established by the GM. Initially no faction controls it.

goals.title: Acquire the Book of Names
goals.progressingWorldState: Aspis obtains a means of entering the Book of Names' current holding site.
goals.completedWorldState: Aspis takes the Book of Names from its current custodian.

goals.title: Steal the Offering Chest
goals.progressingWorldState: Offerings go missing from the Chest inventory and its custody becomes Contested.
goals.completedWorldState: Aspis takes the Offering Chest from its current holder; its gifts cease to be available at Pilgrim's Rest.

goals.title: Abide
goals.progressingWorldState: Cult attendants are admitted to accompany the upcoming Keeper Procession.
goals.completedWorldState: Cult attendants occupy the approaches to the House of Abiding and demand custody; a takeover attempt begins.

goals.title: Connect
goals.progressingWorldState: Pilgrim’s Rest can trace surrendered possessions through Claims Registry entries.
goals.completedWorldState: Cult controls the Claims Registry; new Cult-related Veiled incursions gain +1 Class.

goals.title: Reveal
goals.progressingWorldState: Pilgrim's Rest prepares an exhibition around reports of the missing resonant object.
goals.completedWorldState: The Cult takes the Unclaimed Object from its current holder and exhibits it at Pilgrim's Rest; a Veiled incursion begins around the genuine source.

goals.title: Understand
goals.progressingWorldState: Cult agents prepare to take the Ledger from its current custodian.
goals.completedWorldState: The Cult takes the Ledger from its current holder and brings it to Pilgrim's Rest.

goals.title: Freeze the Civic Improvement Fund
goals.progressingWorldState: The Civic Improvement Fund becomes Contested as EGRESS places payments under review; Dawn-funded construction is interrupted.
goals.completedWorldState: EGRESS takes control of the Civic Improvement Fund and Dawn-funded work remains halted until refinanced.

goals.title: Requisition the Specimen
goals.progressingWorldState: EGRESS identifies the Unclaimed Object's current holder and issues a scientific containment requisition.
goals.completedWorldState: EGRESS takes the Unclaimed Object from its current holder and secures it in Occlusion Containment.

goals.title: Seize the Stockpiles
goals.progressingWorldState: EGRESS locates the Shattered Hidden Stockpiles and begins confiscating them; the network becomes Contested.
goals.completedWorldState: EGRESS seizes the Hidden Stockpiles from their current controller.

goals.title: Break the Shattered
goals.progressingWorldState: The Dead Drop Network becomes Contested as Order patrols identify and loot hidden caches.
goals.completedWorldState: The Dead Drop Network becomes Damaged; new caches contain loot only on 6 (d6).

goals.title: Secure the Procession
goals.progressingWorldState: Order checkpoints restrict access to the Keeper Procession route.
goals.completedWorldState: Armed Order patrols secure all approaches to the Keeper Procession route.

goals.title: Sunset the Dawn
goals.progressingWorldState: A citizen campaign prompts thirty Dawn members to resign (Faction Size −30).
goals.completedWorldState: A further forty Dawn members resign (additional Faction Size −40).

goals.title: Blockade the Procession
goals.progressingWorldState: Dawn demonstrators gather along the Keeper Procession route.
goals.completedWorldState: A civilian blockade obstructs the Keeper Procession route; its eventual passage remains a matter for play.

goals.title: Gain Momentum
goals.progressingWorldState: Dawn campaign posters appear throughout the Assembly district.
goals.completedWorldState: Dawn campaign posters cover public walls and noticeboards across the Colony.

goals.title: Open the Book of Names
goals.progressingWorldState: Dawn agents prepare to take the Book of Names from its current custodian.
goals.completedWorldState: Dawn takes the Book of Names and makes it available for public inspection.

goals.title: Secure the Hall of Keepers
goals.progressingWorldState: During Totality, Dawn stewards establish a Contested presence in the Hall of Keepers.
goals.completedWorldState: Dawn takes control of the Hall of Keepers, displacing Order administration.

goals.title: Sunset the Order
goals.progressingWorldState: A public hearing on Order authority is scheduled at Assembly Hall; a motion to withdraw recognition is introduced.
goals.completedWorldState: Dawn bars Order officials from Assembly Hall unless specifically invited, refusing to recognize their authority inside it.

goals.title: Break the Lectern
goals.progressingWorldState: The Empty Lectern becomes Damaged and is unsafe for remembrance ceremonies.
goals.completedWorldState: The Empty Lectern is Destroyed; remembrance ceremonies require another site or lectern.

goals.title: Silence the Bell
goals.progressingWorldState: The Bell of the Sun becomes Damaged and its ringing is unreliable.
goals.completedWorldState: The Bell of the Sun is Destroyed; the Order loses its civic alarm.

goals.title: Steal the Ledger
goals.progressingWorldState: Shattered operatives obtain access to the Ledger's current holding site.
goals.completedWorldState: The Shattered take the Ledger from its current custodian.

goals.title: Steal the Unclaimed Object
goals.progressingWorldState: Shattered operatives trace the Unclaimed Object to its current holder and prepare a covert theft.
goals.completedWorldState: The Shattered steal the Unclaimed Object from its current holder.

goals.title: Take out the Keeper
goals.progressingWorldState: Tavia Rusk begins shadowing Darkwing, looking for access to Vara.
goals.completedWorldState: During the next session, Tavia Rusk attempts to assassinate Vara; the attempt does not guarantee her death.

goals.title: Empty the Reform Treasury
goals.progressingWorldState: The Civic Improvement Fund becomes Contested as Witnesses divert a grant toward preservation.
goals.completedWorldState: Witnesses take control of the Civic Improvement Fund and redirect its resources toward preservation.

goals.title: Recover the Unclaimed Object
goals.progressingWorldState: Witness recovery notices identify the missing resonant object and offer a reward for its return.
goals.completedWorldState: Witnesses take the Unclaimed Object from its current holder and catalog it at the Hall of Remembrance.

goals.title: Twilight the Dawn
goals.progressingWorldState: Witnesses authenticate Assembly records that contradict a claim in Dawn campaign literature.
goals.completedWorldState: Witnesses paste corrective broadsides over or beside Dawn posters across the Colony, publishing the contradictory records.

locations.name: Abiding Way
locations.description: District maintained by the Witnesses.

locations.name: Assembly Hall
locations.description: The Civic headquarters of the Dawn Assembly.

locations.name: Candlestone Caverns
locations.description: Caverns in the foothills of the Aspodell mountains the lead into the Darklands.

locations.name: Clearing House
locations.description: Aspis administrative building dedicated to reconciling the Colony's debts.

locations.name: Crescent Island
locations.description: The oxbow island within the Colony housing the remains of abandoned structures built before the river changed course.

locations.name: Darkmoon Plains
locations.description: A flood plain in northern Andoran along the Isger border. The River Foam runs from the Five Kings Mountains through it.

locations.name: Dawn District
locations.description: The Dawn Assembly's major civic initiatives are housed here.

locations.name: Dead Drop Network
locations.description: A network of hidden caches and messages used by the Shattered.

locations.name: EGRESS Institute
locations.description: The Engram Generation, Restoration, Evaluation, and Storage Systems Institute campus.

locations.name: Engram Vault
locations.description: Long-term storage for memory-containing Engrams.

locations.name: Hall of Keepers
locations.description: The operational headquarters of the Order of Theia.

locations.name: Hall of Remembrance
locations.description: The Witnesses keep objects here that are imbued with emotional resonance.

locations.name: Hidden Tunnel
locations.description: A hidden tunnel leading to the Ritual Chamber.

locations.name: High Bank
locations.description: Older, more established part of The Colony

locations.name: House of Abiding
locations.description: The residence of the Keeper once Called.

locations.name: Keeper District
locations.description: The center of the Colony.

locations.name: Lower Bank
locations.description: Lower, newer part of the Colony

locations.name: Memorial Building
locations.description: Where the Reading of the Ledger takes place.

locations.name: Mercantile District
locations.description: Warehouses, Docks, and Industrial buildings dominate this part of the Colony.

locations.name: Milltown
locations.description: The heavily populated upper portion of the River.

locations.name: Monument of the First Keeper
locations.description: A monument honoring the First Keeper.

locations.name: Occlusion Containment
locations.description: Institute containment and testing facility for Veiled phenomena.

locations.name: Old Cemetery
locations.description: The Colony's original cemetery.

locations.name: Old Town
locations.description: A portion of the Colony destroyed during a former Veiled incursion. Rebuilding has proven difficult.

locations.name: Pilgrim Quarter
locations.description: The southern portion of the Colony nearest the Duskwood.

locations.name: Pilgrim's Rest
locations.description: An Inn run by the Cult of the Unknown that acts as a waystation for the living and the forgotten.

locations.name: Ritual Chamber
locations.description: A hidden chamber where the Reading is performed.

locations.name: The Broken Bell
locations.description: A Tavern at the edge of Old Town, under an iconic broken bell recovered from the ruins of the Old Wall.

locations.name: The Colony
locations.description: An independent city-state astride the River Foam on the border of Isger and Andoran.

locations.name: The Duskway
locations.description: Between Old Town and more populated districts, people that live in the Duskway live between light and dark.

locations.name: The Duskwood
locations.description: A large forest on Andoran's northern border between the Aspodell Mountains and the River Foam. Situated just north of the Candlestone Caverns, it's filled with unknown dangers.

locations.name: The Garrison
locations.description: Housing, Training, Armory, and Munitions for the Colony Guard.

locations.name: The Manor
locations.description: Abandoned manor in the center of the Colony

locations.name: The Riverfront
locations.description: The High Bank Shore of the River

locations.name: Veiled House
locations.description: A house on Crescent Island that has been long abandoned.

locations.name: West District
locations.description: Expansion occupied mostly by construction efforts and support for the logging industry.

conditions.title: Procession Checkpoints
conditions.rule: Unauthorized passage along the planned procession route requires bypassing Order checkpoints.

conditions.title: Procession Secured
conditions.rule: Armed Order guards control approaches to the Procession.

conditions.title: Procession Blockade
conditions.rule: The occupied route cannot be used without negotiation, dispersal or alternate approach.

conditions.title: Dawn Poster Campaign
conditions.rule: Dawn campaign posters cover the Colony, giving residents clear organizing contacts and public meeting notices.

conditions.title: Cult Procession Access
conditions.rule: Cult attendants may accompany the upcoming Keeper Procession.

conditions.title: House Custody Dispute
conditions.rule: Cult attendants demand custody of House of Abiding; its access may be contested in play.

conditions.title: Witness Specimen
conditions.rule: Witnesses offer supervised examination of the Unclaimed Object at the Hall.

conditions.title: Pilgrims Rest Incursion
conditions.rule: An active Veiled incursion affects Pilgrim's Rest and may require containment.

conditions.title: Cult Registry Pattern
conditions.rule: New Cult-related Veiled incursions gain +1 Class (stacks with Cult Ledger Relationships; max Class V; not retroactive).

conditions.title: Cult Ledger Relationships
conditions.rule: New Cult-related Veiled incursions gain +1 Class (stacks with Cult Registry Pattern; max Class V; not retroactive).

conditions.title: Pilgrims Gifts
conditions.rule: Maelyn can offer gifts from surrendered possessions.

conditions.title: Registry Arrangement
conditions.rule: Perrik can provide services connecting Cult-related surrendered property to the Claims Registry.

conditions.title: Public Access to the Book
conditions.rule: Dawn makes the Book available for public inspection, without automatically identifying the people named.

conditions.title: Public Works Funded
conditions.rule: Dawn controls the Civic Improvement Fund and it is neither Contested nor Destroyed: Dawn-funded projects proceed.

conditions.title: Public Works Disrupted
conditions.rule: New Dawn-funded projects cannot begin; existing work pauses unless refinanced.

conditions.title: Order Excluded
conditions.rule: Order officials cannot enter Assembly Hall as authorities without a Dawn invitation.

conditions.title: The Record Corrected
conditions.rule: Witness-authenticated historical accounts appear on broadsides covering or accompanying Dawn posters, and remain usable as evidence.

conditions.title: Displaced Administration
conditions.rule: Dawn occupies the civic offices; Order administrators operate elsewhere or regain access.

conditions.title: Cache Looting
conditions.rule: Newly discovered caches hold loot on Stable 4–6; Contested 5–6; Damaged 6 only; Destroyed none (d6).

conditions.title: Remembrance Disrupted
conditions.rule: Witnesses cannot use the Empty Lectern for customary rites; must find an alternative.

conditions.title: Bell Unreliable / Silent
conditions.rule: If Damaged, ringing unreliable; if Destroyed, no civic ringing from this Bell.

conditions.title: Civic Alarm Lost
conditions.rule: Loss of the Colony's familiar civic alarm increases public unease.

conditions.title: Supplies Confiscated
conditions.rule: The Shattered cannot draw equipment and consumables from the confiscated network.
